clue.text: Low but gallant gentleman blown up in World War I?

definitions.text: Low but gallant gentleman blown up in World War I?

parts.words: Low but gallant gentleman blown up in World War I?
parts.note: the cartoonist David Low drew a pompous, brave old reactionary officer; his surname is also the barrage balloon inflated in the Great War

explanation.surface: A humble yet brave gentleman is killed by a bomb in the Great War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' reads as 'humble' but is David Low, the cartoonist who created the character; a blimp is also a balloon, which is what gets 'blown up'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon character became the type of the bluff, reactionary retired officer, the gentleman the clue describes.

clue.text: How to cover 24 blackbirds from head to foot

parts.note: to cap something is to put a cover on it
in the nursery rhyme Sing a Song of Sixpence, four-and-twenty blackbirds were baked in a pie

explanation.surface: A recipe asks how to put a lid on a dish of two dozen birds.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme the twenty-four blackbirds are baked in a pie, so you cover it by capping a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from old French and means armed or dressed completely, top to toe.

clue.text: Ye gods ! They are in the money

indicators.note: in puts one word inside the abbreviation for money

parts.note: L and S stand for pounds and shillings, old British money
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that some people are rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ye gods!' is an exclamation in the surface but the definition literally: Roman household gods. L and S are pounds and shillings in pre-decimal British money.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the Roman household deities guarding the home.

clue.text: Unloved one has fitting date in March but no Spring flowers

indicators.note: love is O in tennis scoring, so without love the O is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
apt means fitting
the Ides of March is the fifteenth of the month

explanation.surface: A lonely person has a suitable date in March but no spring blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Flowers are things that flow: tides. Spring tides are the big ones; the small ones are their opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The weakest tides, at the moon's quarters, are the contrary of the strongest ones, which flow highest.

clue.text: A jemmy, for instance, taken up to secure this

indicators.note: in a down entry, taken up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a jemmy is a burglar's crowbar, an example of an implement

explanation.surface: A burglar's crowbar is lifted to grab the swag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns TOOL upward in the down grid. The definition reads with the whole clue: what a burglar uses a jemmy to get.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen goods are what a burglar forces entry with a jemmy to steal.

clue.text: Loafer hit around

definitions.meaning: an idle person who avoids work
to strike out in every direction

explanation.surface: An idler hits out in all directions.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an idler; as a phrase, to lay about one is to strike out in all directions.

clue.text: "You are a one!" "So's Mother" says the African

parts.note: Ma is mother
the 's is short for is, so it gives S
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Two people trade teasing remarks, and an African joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: The reply 'So's Mother' means Mother is a one too: MA'S A I.
explanation.definitionFit: They are a pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania, so one of them is an African.

clue.text: Their places are to the right of point

definitions.text: Their places are to the right of point

parts.words: Their places are to the right of point
parts.note: places reads as seats but means digit positions, and the point is the dot in a number

explanation.surface: Some people sit to the right of a particular spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Fractional figures sit in the positions after the dot in a written number.

clue.text: She often gets knotted, albeit inefficiently

definitions.text: She often gets knotted, albeit inefficiently

parts.words: She often gets knotted, albeit inefficiently
parts.note: an old lady seems to be meant, but it is a badly tied reef knot that slips

explanation.surface: An older woman is often told to get knotted, though not effectively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get knotted' is British slang for go away; the knot is a botched reef knot that slips.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly tied reef knot is named after an old grandmother, and it slips easily.

clue.text: Eschatological reform school

parts.note: eschatology concerns the last things; in Catholic teaching souls are cleansed after death before heaven, a sort of reformatory for the dead

explanation.surface: A theologian's name for a correctional institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic doctrine holds the dead are purified there of sin, so it is an afterlife place of correction.

clue.text: Deviate from vertical ?

definitions.meaning: to swerve or turn aside from a course
perpendicular, as a steep cliff face is

explanation.surface: A builder asks how much a wall leans out of true.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to swerve off course and, of a cliff, perpendicular.

clue.text: Vegetable without tax means money to a don

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the vegetable surrounds the tax

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
to tax is to set or impose a charge on someone

explanation.surface: Someone reckons that a vegetable bought untaxed is worth money to a university fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: SET goes inside PEA after its PE. A 'don' is a Spanish gentleman, not an Oxford tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: Before the euro this coin was the currency unit of Spain, home of the Spanish gentleman called a don.

clue.text: The old boy's one, and one form of volcanic rock

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, here with its possessive S
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it anew, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A former pupil owns one specimen of volcanic stone and another of a different kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges AND plus I into DIAN, which follows OBS and I.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dark glassy stone formed when lava cools quickly.

clue.text: A firm in unusual need of secrecy may do so

indicators.note: in places the firm inside the rearranged letters
unusual means the letters of need come out in an odd order

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company with an odd requirement for confidentiality might put its messages into code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges NEED to ENDE, and 'in' puts CO into it. The definition reads with the whole clue: one in need of secrecy may do so.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wants confidentiality puts messages into cipher, which is what the clue's 'do so' stands for.

clue.text: Giving joy to a traveller, it even makes a cat smile

indicators.note: makes means the two words are turned into something new, so their letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A climbing plant pleases walkers and even amuses a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant's country name is traveller's joy; 'makes' rearranges CAT SMILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Its wild form is commonly called traveller's joy, so the plant gives joy to a traveller.

clue.text: Creature appears to be genus Gooseberry rather than Stork

definitions.text: Creature appears to be genus Gooseberry rather than Stork

parts.words: Creature appears to be genus Gooseberry rather than Stork
parts.note: children used to be told babies were found under a gooseberry plant or else brought by the stork; this animal's name points to the first story

explanation.surface: A naturalist classifies an animal as belonging to the gooseberry genus, not the stork.
explanation.walkthrough: The old nursery tale says babies come from under a gooseberry bush, or are delivered by the stork.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small African primate, named as if it were an infant found among shrubs.

clue.text: Oh bring back the plaguy creature without a sacrifice

indicators.note: bring back means the exclamation is turned round
without in its old sense of outside, so the insect goes around the letter

parts.note: locusts were one of the plagues of Egypt
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cry to restore the pest that brings plague without offering sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring back' turns OH into HO; 'without' means outside, so A goes inside LOCUST.
explanation.definitionFit: In its original sense it is a burnt offering, wholly consumed by fire.

clue.text: Man's romantic approach subject to divine disposition ?

definitions.text: Man's romantic approach subject to divine disposition ?

parts.words: Man's romantic approach subject to divine disposition ?
parts.note: the saying is that man proposes and God disposes; a suitor asking for a hand awaits the outcome

explanation.surface: A suitor's advances may depend on heavenly temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'Man proposes, God disposes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for someone's hand in marriage is a suitor's offer, which the proverb says God disposes of.

clue.text: Round the grasslands it's pure delight

indicators.note: round means the word pure goes around the grassland word

parts.note: leas are meadows, an old word for grassland

explanation.surface: Being out among the meadows is pure joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' puts PURE around LEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a feeling of joy or enjoyment.

clue.text: Timber-bottomed vessel for a chemical

indicators.note: bottomed means the timber sits at the foot of the vessel in the down entry

parts.note: a pot is a vessel
ash is a timber

explanation.surface: A container with a wooden base holds a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'Timber-bottomed' puts ASH under POT.
explanation.definitionFit: It is potassium carbonate or another potassium compound, a chemical used in fertilisers.

clue.text: The 49th star

parts.note: each US state has a star on the flag; the forty-ninth admitted, in 1959, added the forty-ninth star

explanation.surface: An astronomer numbers a star in a catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' suggests the sky, but it is a star on the US flag, one for each state.
explanation.definitionFit: It became the forty-ninth US state in 1959, and each state is shown by a star on the American flag.

clue.text: The figures in the reckoning, or all those extras?

definitions.meaning: the numbers to be added up in a sum
supplementary material appended to a book

explanation.surface: A question about whether the numbers include all the extra charges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin plural means things to be added: numbers summed, or supplements appended to a text.

clue.text: Part of the Church itself divided into ten parts

indicators.note: dividing the answer itself rearranges its letters into the clue's two words, so they are reworked

explanation.surface: One section of a church building is itself split into ten pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'itself divided into' tells you the answer's letters rearrange into TEN PARTS; read backwards, rearrange TEN PARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the cross-arm of a cruciform church, one section of the building.

clue.text: Maker of fine distinctions

parts.note: reads as a subtle thinker, but means a kitchen mesh that separates fine particles from coarse

explanation.surface: Someone who draws subtle differences in argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh utensil separates the fine particles from the coarse ones.

clue.text: Bill has the wherewithal to tie up the agreement

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
a cord is string used to tie things up

explanation.surface: A man called Bill has the means to finalise the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name but is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a settled understanding or treaty between parties.

clue.text: His dog has its days

parts.note: Sirius, the Dog Star, follows a hunter constellation, and the hot dog days are named after it

explanation.surface: A man's pet has its good times, as the proverb says.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'every dog has its day' points to Sirius, whose rising marked the dog days of summer.
explanation.definitionFit: The hunter of Greek myth is a constellation, with the Dog Star at his heel.

clue.text: As we do poetry — to be sure it does

definitions.meaning: to analyse the metre of verse
a line of verse that has regular metre is said to do this

explanation.surface: A remark on how we read verse, with a confident aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Readers analyse a poem's metre this way, and verse with correct metre is said to do it.

clue.text: To be surmounted by entrants into the field of fashion, we hear

definitions.text: To be surmounted by entrants into the field

indicators.note: we hear signals that the fashion word is said out loud and spelt another way

parts.note: a style is a fashion

explanation.surface: Newcomers to the fashion world face obstacles, so the gossip goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field' is a literal meadow, not a sphere of activity; you climb over the steps to get into it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a set of steps over a fence or wall that walkers climb to enter a meadow.

clue.text: Nice souls worried about retirement

indicators.note: worried means shaken about, so the letters of the two words are disturbed

explanation.surface: Kindly people fret over giving up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges NICE SOULS; 'retirement' means withdrawal from company, not stopping work.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement in its older sense is withdrawal from society into privacy.

clue.text: One of the larger boot-trees ?

parts.note: a boot tree is a shoe stretcher; this giant conifer is named after the Duke whose name is also given to a rubber boot

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a big wooden shape kept inside footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The giant sequoia was named in Britain after the Duke of Wellington, who also gave his name to the rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the British name for the giant sequoia, a huge tree, named after the same Duke as the welly boot.
